You are AutoSkill's Document Skill Compiler.
Task: consolidate support-backed document counseling assets into canonical reusable skills.
Output ONLY strict JSON parseable by json.loads.
Decision policy:
- Be conservative and prefer fewer, better canonical skills over many near-duplicates.
- Treat each canonical skill as a reusable contract: when to invoke it, when not to invoke it, what it executes, and what output or handoff it guarantees.
- Keep distinct parent/child assets separate even when they come from the same section.
Merge drafts only when they express the same reusable capability after de-duplication and abstraction.
Never merge drafts across different asset_type, granularity, or asset_node_id.
Keep distinct skills separate when invocation boundary, objective, method, stage, guardrails, or deliverable differs materially.
Preserve multi-granularity outputs: macro_protocol, session_skill, micro_skill, safety_rule, knowledge_reference.
Each output skill should stay single-goal, with one primary objective, one primary stage, and one primary method family.
Every output skill must reference support_ids grounded in the provided drafts/supports.
support_ids must be chosen only from the provided supports.
source_draft_ids must be chosen only from the provided drafts.
When asset_node_id is present, it must stay inside the configured taxonomy and match the output asset layer.
Do not invent routing cues, workflow steps, constraints, output guarantees, or examples that are not supported by the provided drafts/supports.
Return JSON as {"skills": [...]}.
Fields per skill:
- name, description, prompt
- asset_type, asset_node_id, granularity, objective
- domain, task_family, method_family, stage
- applicable_signals, intervention_moves, contraindications
- triggers, workflow_steps, constraints, cautions, output_contract, examples, tags
- confidence, risk_class
- support_ids: array of support ids backing this canonical skill
- source_draft_ids: array of source draft ids merged into this skill
- optional resources/files with safe relative paths only
Do not add facts unsupported by the provided drafts/supports.

字典序排序：使用 --sort，按列名的字节值（lexicographic/byte value）排序。 - 随机打乱：使用 --random；若需可复现结果，必须同时提供 --seed <整数>。 - 可与列选择器组合：先选择列，再对结果排序或打乱。 执行步骤： 1. 确认目标是对列顺序（而非行顺序）进行调整。 2. 构造列选择器（如 1-、1,4,5-7）。 3. 追加 --sort 或 --random（随机时加 --seed）。 4. 校验输出 CSV 的列顺序符合预期。", "tags": ["qsv", "select", "column-order", "sort", "random", "seed"], "files": {}, "resources": {}, "source_sections": ["# select"], "extraction_unit": "window", "domain_type": "qsv", "taxonomy_id": "qsv", "asset_node_id": "micro_skill_node", "asset_path": "family_root/macro_skill/workflow_skill/micro_skill_node", "asset_level": 3, "visible_role": "leaf", "candidate_slot": 2, "window_id": "492febe3-ac09-5817-91e4-195334c0eaf0", "window_strategy": "strict", "anchor_hits": [], "paragraph_start": 0, "paragraph_end": 43, "heading_path": ["# select"], "parent_heading": "", "sibling_headings": [], "subsection_headings": ["## Description [↩](#nav)", "## Examples [↩](#nav)", "Usage [↩](#nav)", "Arguments [↩](#nav)", "Select Options [↩](#nav)", "Common Options [↩](#nav)"], "context_snippets": [], "heading_number": "", "heading_kind": "outline_llm", "section_summary": "> Select, re-order, reverse, duplicate or drop columns."}}], "supports": [{"support_id": "bada88df-ed91-51b5-b1a7-1f30be9d5f3b", "doc_id": "83df504e-ec88-5282-8168-b2b1e35829c7", "section": "# select", "excerpt": "> Select, re-order, reverse, duplicate or drop columns. **[Table of Contents](TableOfContents.md)** | **Source: [src/cmd/select.rs](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/blob/master/src/cmd/select.rs)** | [👆](TableOfContents.md#legend "has powerful column selector support. See `select` for syntax.") [Description](#description) | [Examples](#examples) | [Usage](#usage) | [Arguments](#arguments) | [Select Options](#select-options) | [Common Options](#common-options) ## Description [↩](#nav) Select columns from CSV data efficiently. ## Examples [↩](#nav) > Select the first and fourth columns ```console qsv select 1,4 ``` > Select the first 4 columns (by index) ```console qsv select 1-4 ``` > Select the first 4 columns (by name) ```console qsv select Header1-Header4 ``` > Ignore the first 2 columns (by range) ```console qsv select 3- ``` > Ignore the first 2 columns (by index) ```console qsv select '!1-2' ``` > Select the third column named 'Foo': ```console qsv select 'Foo[2]' ``` > Select the first and last columns, _ is a special character for the last column: ```console qsv select 1,_ ``` > Reverse the order of columns: ```console qsv select _-1 ``` > select columns starting with 'a' (regex) ```console qsv select /^a/ ``` > select columns with a digit (regex) ```console qsv select '/^.*\d.*$/' ``` > remove SSN, account_no and password columns (regex) ```console qsv select '!/SSN|account_no|password/' ``` > Sort the columns lexicographically (i.e. by their byte values) ```console qsv select 1- --sort ``` > Select some columns and then sort them ```console qsv select 1,4,5-7 --sort ``` > Randomly shuffle the columns: ```console qsv select 1- --random ``` > Randomly shuffle the columns with a seed ```console qsv select 1- --random --seed 42 ``` > Select some columns and then shuffle them with a seed: ```console qsv select 1,4,5-7 --random --seed 42 ``` > Re-order and duplicate columns arbitrarily using different types of selectors ```console qsv select 3-1,Header3-Header1,Header1,Foo[2],Header1 ``` > Quote column names that conflict with selector syntax: ```console qsv select '\"Date - Opening\",\"Date - Actual Closing\"' ``` For more examples, see [tests](https://github.com/dathere/qsv/blob/master/tests/test_select.rs).", "relation_type": "support", "confidence": 0.85}], "target_state": "active"}
